title: One-dimensional Bloch, Wannier, and tight-binding reduction exercise
status_detail: Human accepted and closed. The controlled isolated-band, adversarial, direct composite-band, and converged preconditioned Wannier90 results are retained with passing declared verifiers, reports, and figures. The failed preprocessing and nonconverged localization attempts remain explicit evidence rather than being reclassified. Acceptance retains the 2.63e-3-cell higher-pair center discrepancy, weak external isolation, synthetic transverse embedding, and optimizer sensitivity as limitations. It establishes completion of this synthetic-model numerical-verification Task; semiconductor validation, scientific validation, UQ, additional external execution, and successor activation are not claimed.
objective: Develop the one-dimensional cosine-lattice exercise spanning Bloch fibers, independent plane-wave and real-space representations, retained subspaces, localization, hopping reconstruction, and direct-versus-mediated tight-binding reduction.
authorized_scope: Plan independently refined plane-wave and finite-difference Bloch representations with exact symmetry and perturbative checks.
Transport representations into common low-mode or retained-band coordinates before operator comparison.
Develop isolated- and composite-band gauge, localization, hopping-range, withheld-data, and direct-versus-mediated reduction exercises one controlled complication at a time.
completion_criteria: Parent-representation, reciprocal-sampling, retained-subspace, gauge, localization, hopping-truncation, fitting, and observable-extraction errors remain separately reported.
Reconstruction, symmetry, projector, overlap-conditioning, and route-comparison checks are executable under frozen illustrative inputs.
Any optional comparison with Wannier90 requires separate execution authority and remains numerical verification of the cosine model, not material validation.
exclusions: No silicon-specific parent, Quantum ESPRESSO execution, production Wannierization, scientific validation, or public scientific API freeze is authorized.
Agreement between two unconverged representations is not accepted as convergence.
The tight-binding model is not described as converging directly to the scalar potential.
